problem_type: Native model media capability is lost between project attachments and provider requests
symptom: Audio/video attachments reach a full-modality model as identity text rather than original media, despite the provider accepting native media.
direct_cause: Agent skips audio/video bytes, model call content is text/image only, and provider assembly exposes no Google-native transport.
class_root: The shared model input contract has no typed original media representation or capability-aware serialization boundary.
affected_population: Agent users attaching audio or video
Single-shot text tasks with original audio/video references

external_sources.purpose: Native inline media parts and generation schema
Audio input shape for compatible protocol
Supported custom fetch hook preserves Nomi network boundary

invariants: Declared original media arrives byte-for-byte in the supported provider request.
Unsupported, unreadable or over-limit media is rejected before dispatch, never summarized or silently omitted.
Persisted conversations contain original asset identities rather than inline media data.
Existing text/image/PDF and tool-call behavior retains the same owner boundaries.

door_reduction.why_not: Existing Agent, one-shot, configuration, discovery and renderer surfaces remain distinct user entry points. The generated door map covers their shared input/capability/provider boundaries; none needs a second protocol implementation.

generality_proof: Capabilities are explicit model metadata, not model-name matching. Typed media, validation and payload rewriting are shared across Agent and one-shot callers and use protocol dispatch rather than relay-specific code.

shared_boundaries.responsibility: Original file payloads, protocol support and aggregate encoded-size validation
Resolve per-model protocol and declared input modalities
Reuse provider stream and Nomi network/cancellation/error boundaries

same_class_entry_points.evidence: Original attached identities become typed media before provider serialization; history reconstructed from the same path.
Native file input is bound and serialized through the same payload boundary.
Single-shot original reference media is represented with the same typed input.
Original canonical attachment claims are retained across compaction and rehydrated after restart; text summaries do not replace originals.

recurrence.reason: Every audio/video input to any full-modality custom model reaches these shared boundaries.

prevention.invariant: Every declared original media part is serialized or rejected explicitly before network dispatch.
prevention.failure_mode: Typed error names unsupported/unreadable/over-limit media; no reference-only analysis fallback.
prevention.strategy: Shared typed content and payload encoder for native files; stable provider protocol contracts and explicit input capabilities.

legacy_paths.rationale: Remove audio/video skip-and-reference behavior for native input; existing PDF entry is delegated to the shared file serializer.

dependency_lifecycle.target: @google/genai 2.32.0 with narrowly patched pi-ai 0.85.1 Google fetch forwarding
dependency_lifecycle.rationale: Reuse the mature SDK/stream/tool/history implementation and its supported fetch option instead of introducing an independent engine.
exit_criteria: Remove pi patch when upstream forwards custom fetch; run native transport and tool/history tests against the replacement.

migration: Additive optional model metadata. Existing connections retain saved protocol and image/PDF behavior; users select native protocol and explicitly declare audio/video input. Project asset identifiers remain unchanged.
residual_risks: Real relay compatibility must be verified separately from loopback serialization.
Inline media is bounded to 20 MiB encoded request size; large provider-file upload is not implemented.
Google SDK minor upgrade and provider tool/thought replay require focused regression verification.
